plugin.name: Browser Use
plugin.description: Let the agent drive a real browser: navigate, read pages, fill forms, click and sign in.
view.console.label: Browser Use
view.console.description: Browser runtime status and how to use it
hero.tagline: Let the agent actually open a browser, click through pages and fill forms — instead of handing back a summary of the web.
console.title: Browser Use
console.installHint: First install the browser automation runtime. Chrome for Testing is needed only for a separate task browser when system Chrome is unavailable.
console.outdatedHint: Found agent-browser {{found}}, but this plugin needs {{required}} or newer. Upgrade installs the pinned version into 567 Agent's own runtime directory and leaves your existing global install untouched.
console.chromeFound: System Chrome is available for separate task windows. Connecting to an existing window still requires selecting the target and approving access.
console.chromeMissing: A separate task window needs Chrome for Testing. Connecting to an existing browser requires its local connection settings.
console.readyHint: The runtime is available. It connects to your existing browser and verifies the tab first. A separate task browser must be explicitly requested. First-time connection may require enabling local remote debugging and approving access in the browser.
guide.capabilities.label: What it can do
guide.cap.navigate.title: Open a page and actually read it
guide.cap.navigate.body: Navigate anywhere and locate elements through an accessibility-tree snapshot — cheaper on context than screenshots, more precise than raw HTML.
guide.cap.interact.title: Really operate the page
guide.cap.interact.body: Use page elements for clicking, forms and scrolling. Canvas areas can use viewport screenshots and page coordinates, followed by result verification.
guide.cap.signin.title: Use your current browser login
guide.cap.signin.body: Connect to an existing tab first. Complete verification yourself. Cookies are not copied; explicitly request a separate browser for an independent account environment.
guide.cap.isolation.title: Isolated accounts
guide.cap.isolation.body: Control sessions bind separate tabs. An attached browser shares your login state; independent profiles are used only for explicitly requested separate browsers.
guide.vs.label: How this differs from web search
guide.vs.body: Web search returns someone else's summary. It cannot open pages behind a login and cannot change anything. Browser Use opens a real browser: it can get into an admin panel, fill a form, page through to result 3 and export what it finds. Use search to look something up; use this to get something done.
guide.prompts.label: Try saying
guide.prompts.hint: Click to copy, then adapt it to your case.
guide.prompt.read: Open https://news.ycombinator.com and use a snapshot to put the top 10 titles and links into a table.
guide.prompt.signin: Connect to the orders tab in my current browser, verify the page and summarize this month’s orders. Let me complete any verification.
guide.prompt.form: Open this signup form and fill it in with the details below, but don't submit — let me review first: name Jane Doe, email jane@example.com.
guide.prompt.compare: Open these two product pages and compare price, stock and estimated delivery in one table.
guide.cli.label: CLI execution
guide.cli.direct: The agent calls agent-browser directly through the shell without loading an additional browser-specific Tool.
guide.cli.independent: Each task has its own control session and verifies its target tab, without silently switching to another task or user page.
guide.cli.accounts: For separate task browsers, use different session suffixes and restore keys for independent account state.
guide.cli.upstream: For complex operations the agent reads the core skill bundled with the installed version, avoiding command-reference drift.
guide.cli.hint: Connection failures are explained instead of silently launching another browser. Your browser and tabs stay open when the task ends.
guide.newSession: Connect to the current browser by default. To use a separate environment, ask for an independent task browser.
footer.credit: Browser automation is provided by vercel-labs/agent-browser (Apache-2.0). This plugin installs the runtime and contributes its CLI Skill to the agent.
